newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics comfortable with 1997 estimates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics comfortable with 1997 estimates.

text.p: A senior U.S. Robotics Corp executive said the company is comfortable with Wall Street estimates of $3.20-$3.30 earnings per share and around $3 billion in revenues for its fiscal 1997.

"We're comfortable with the range of estimates that's out on the Street -- roughly $3 billion in revenue and (earnings per share of $3.20 to the low $3.30s," U.S. Robotics Chief Operating Officer John McCartney told Reuters after a presentation to investors at the Montgomery Securities TechnologyWeek conference here.
McCartney declined to discuss its current first fiscal quarter. The company's fiscal year ends September 30.
Skokie, Illinois-based U.S. Robotics is the dominant provider of desktop modems and a leader in remote access analog and ISDN products for both customers and the Internet service providers.
"We believe that we'll be able to continue to outperform other people in terms of both absolute dollar and percentage revenue for companies that have that kind of scale," he said.
"We think that some of our competitors have done a magnificent job in building their businesses, but they will face the same challenges as they get larger."

McCartney challenged what he said was misleading market share information provided by unnamed competitors which he said had exaggerated rivals' market share, citing data for the worldwide remote access solutions market showing "that our share is just about 40 percent and it's the largest."

"Our business is at the boundary," the executive said, referring to its approach to providing products for both the people connecting remotely and connecting into service providers' networks, but not core networking products.

"Our business is to build the on-ramps and off-ramps of the Information Superhighway," McCartney told investors in his presentation, which included a briefing on the company's new x2 technology that increases the speed of a standard modem for downloading data to 56 kilobits per second.
Higher-end modems for regular telephone lines now operate at a top speed of 28.8 or 33.6 kilobits per second.

McCartney noted that the U.S. Robotics breakthrough would provide the enhanced capability for those who used the technology at both ends of the line, adding the company has worked to make its products software upgradeable.
"We believe that we are significantly ahead," with the technology, he added.
